clue.text: Scholarly woman unhappy keeping things to sell

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling unhappy
a shop stocking goods is keeping them in for sale

explanation.surface: A learned woman is miserable about holding on to items she should be selling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' looks like a container signal, but it belongs to the phrase 'keeping things to sell', which is simply STOCKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluestocking is an old, often disparaging, term for an intellectual or literary woman.

clue.text: Opponents splitting suit to advantage

indicators.note: the opponents divide the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: to suit is to befit
E and N are opposing partnerships at bridge (East and North sit against each other's partners)

explanation.surface: Rival parties fighting over a lawsuit to gain an edge.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play East-West, so any two adjacent compass points, here E and N, can stand for opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit is a gain or advantage you get from something.

clue.text: Realise expert can be taken in

parts.note: to realise something is to understand it
an able person is skilled or expert

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a specialist is easily fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being deceived, but here it means mentally grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comprehensible is one the mind can absorb, as in 'I can't take it all in'.

clue.text: Young man in shoot

definitions.meaning: an old word for a youth or young fellow
a small shoot or twig of a plant

explanation.surface: A youth caught up in a shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a lad (somewhat dated) and a little stem of a plant carry this name.

clue.text: Neat speech acceptable for a lunch

definitions.note: describes a dish that may be served as a midday meal, standing for the food itself

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a tongue is a language or manner of speaking

explanation.surface: A tidy address that goes down well at a lunch gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an archaic noun for cattle, not the adjective tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooked ox tongue is a traditional cold meat served at lunch, so the description fits the dish.

clue.text: Keep a tight rein, they say, on crawler here

indicators.note: signals that the word spoken is heard, not seen

parts.note: to curb is to restrain or keep a tight rein on

explanation.surface: Advice to keep firm control over a slow creature.
explanation.walkthrough: A kerb-crawler is a driver who cruises slowly along the roadside edge soliciting; 'crawler' sounds like a baby or insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside edge is where a kerb-crawler drives slowly, so it is the crawler's place.

clue.text: The lion I caught, trained from an early age

indicators.note: a trained animal has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lion has been captured and taught tricks since it was young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from an early age' reads as 'since childhood' but means from the early Stone Age.
explanation.definitionFit: Neolithic describes the New Stone Age, an early period of human history.

clue.text: Mediator having bother with nose after beginning to snuffle

indicators.note: the nose piece comes after the opening letter

parts.note: bother means trouble

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: hooter is slang for a nose

explanation.surface: A peacemaker is having a hard time because of a sniffly nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is someone brought in to settle disputes or solve problems.

clue.text: Develop loom

definitions.meaning: to develop is to come into existence or emerge
to loom is to come into view, often threateningly

explanation.surface: An instruction about building up a weaving frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Both emerging gradually and showing up large on the horizon mean coming into view.

clue.text: More exposed, moving under

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone sheds more clothing as they shift beneath the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuder is the comparative of nude, meaning more bare or uncovered.

clue.text: Jet engine fantastic, but poor PR

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful or wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jet engine is wonderful, but its publicity is weak.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop is a jet turbine engine that drives a propeller.

clue.text: Searching for food in spite of getting older

parts.note: for can mean despite, as in 'for all his faults'
aging means growing older

explanation.surface: Hunting for food even though one is growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Foraging is rummaging around for provisions, as animals do.

clue.text: Note taken in a sort of hand

definitions.meaning: a record jotted down of a meeting
one of the hands on a clock face, the one that counts the smallest units

explanation.surface: A memo jotted down in a particular style of handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' suggests handwriting, but it is a clock hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written memorandum and a clock pointer both take this word.

clue.text: Fairy queen without a sign of doubt is in her element

indicators.note: the letter is left out of the queen's name

parts.note: Titania is queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
um is a hesitant noise expressing doubt

explanation.surface: The fairy queen, quite certain, is in her natural surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in her element' reads as an idiom for being comfortable, but 'element' is the definition, a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a metallic chemical element, symbol Ti.

clue.text: A genuine wife is unusual in a Pacific island

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A truly authentic wife is a rarity on a South Seas island.
explanation.definitionFit: New Guinea is a large island in the south-west Pacific, north of Australia.

clue.text: Unending intestinal infection causing irascibility

indicators.note: the disease's name loses its final letter

parts.note: cholera is a severe bacterial infection of the intestine

explanation.surface: A never-ending stomach bug makes a patient bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Choler is an old word for anger, once thought caused by yellow bile.

clue.text: White trousers, say, good for nothing at Lord's

parts.note: ducks are trousers of white cotton or linen duck
e.g. means 'for example', as 'say' does

explanation.surface: Cricket whites are worthless at the famous London ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground; a batsman out for nothing scores a duck, also called a duck's egg.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a duck's egg means a score of zero, the shape of the figure 0.

clue.text: Distinction about a proper name, say

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: signals that the next piece is heard rather than written

parts.note: a proper name is a proper noun

explanation.surface: Fame concerns an appropriate title, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or distinction earned through achievement.

clue.text: Cover missing wicket, striker survives

indicators.note: the letter for wicket is absent from the covering word

parts.note: a wrapper is a cover or packaging
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at cover misses a chance at the wicket and the batsman survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'survives' is a link word: what is left after the deletion is the answer. 'Cover' and 'striker' are cricket terms in the surface; a rapper is a door knocker.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapper is a door knocker, something that strikes the door.

clue.text: Sort of hedge an astute group forms

parts.note: quick means sharp-witted or astute
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A clever collective creates a type of hedging strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickset is a hedge grown from living cuttings, typically hawthorn.

clue.text: The right book for generating heat

parts.note: Mal is the abbreviation for Malachi, a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: The correct manual for producing warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal means relating to or producing heat.

clue.text: Tablet for a dental condition

definitions.meaning: a flat inscribed slab fixed to a wall
the film of bacteria that builds up on teeth

explanation.surface: A pill prescribed for a problem with teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' suggests a pill, but it is a commemorative slab.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall plaque is a memorial tablet, and dental plaque is deposit on teeth.

clue.text: Part of nursery, perhaps, where runners bound along

definitions.text: Part of nursery, perhaps, where runners bound along

parts.words: Part of nursery, perhaps, where runners bound along
parts.note: a beginners' run on a mountain is called the nursery slope, and the runners are skis gliding down it rather than athletes leaping

explanation.surface: A section of a children's nursery where kids race about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' are skis, and a nursery slope is the gentle run for beginners.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery slope is the easiest kind of piste, an example of the place skiers descend.

clue.text: Journalist in hospital chair

indicators.note: the journalist is placed inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is laid up in a hospital chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair is an enclosed seat carried on poles.

clue.text: Covering round open-air pool

parts.note: a lid is a covering
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cover going over an outdoor swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public outdoor swimming pool.

clue.text: Rose and Len eating out

indicators.note: out means not in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rose and Len are dining at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' poses as a woman's name beside Len; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose.

clue.text: Information given to the Romans

definitions.meaning: a single piece of data or a fact

explanation.surface: Facts handed over to the ancient Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to the Romans' means 'given' in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is one item of data, and in Latin the word means a thing given.

clue.text: Two officers meeting Stanley, the modern model of one

definitions.text: Stanley, the modern model of one
definitions.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's character in The Pirates of Penzance sings that he is the very model of a modern officer of this rank

parts.note: a major and a general are both army officers
a major and a general are both army officers

explanation.surface: Two officers meet a man named Stanley, who is a modern ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: Major-General Stanley in The Pirates of Penzance sings 'I am the very model of a modern Major-General'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gilbert and Sullivan character Stanley holds this rank and calls himself its model example.
